newsitem.title: USA: Europe can't blame jobless on globalization - WTO.
newsitem.headline: Europe can't blame jobless on globalization - WTO.

text.p: The high level of unemployment in Europe cannot be blamed on the globalization process, but rather on the economic policies of European countries, World Trade Organisation Director-General, Renato Ruggiero, said on Sunday.

"Unemployment in Europe is the effect of European economic policies and not of globalization" Ruggiero, who was attending the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, told reporters.
"In the U.S., globalization translates into the creation of an enormous amount of jobs. Europe instead is at the end of the train in both globalization and employment," Ruggiero said.

Ruggiero said the next step is to figure out "where we want to go. Whether we want to create three or four large regional areas in the world, or rather work for a single area, disciplined by rules and by the capacity of making those rules respected."
Ruggiero concluded: "We want a rational, non chaotic world, where relations are not governed merely by power and force."
